I am 53 years old, I never went to school, and I have farmed these seven *mu* in Quzhou County since I was a boy. I know this land with my hands, not with books. This year, like every year, I will plant winter wheat and then summer maize. That is what every household around me does, and the grain buyers always come for it. You do not change a system that has fed your family for decades.

For the wheat, I will rotary-till the soil in October before sowing. I will buy improved seeds from the supply shop—maybe *Luyuan 502*, the same kind my neighbors trust. For each *mu*, I will spread about 100 kg of compound fertilizer as a base, and when the wheat starts jointing in the spring, I will topdress it with urea. I will irrigate three times: once before winter so the crop survives the cold, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I will also spray pesticides four times—herbicide first, then insecticide and fungicide—to keep the crop clean. If the weather is fair, I should harvest about 500 kg per *mu*.

As soon as I cut the wheat in early June, I will sow hybrid maize—*Denghai 605*—straight into the wheat stubble without tilling. There is no time to plough; the summer season is short, and the stubble helps hold the moisture. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing, irrigate twice during the summer, and spray pesticides three times. I expect about 550 kg per *mu* from the maize.

This is my plan because it is the only plan I know, and it works.
